question:
(i) Explain why equipotential surfaces in a uniform electric field are equally spaced for equal differences of potential.
(ii) In a uniform electric field of magnitude $2.5 \times 10^3\text{ V m}^{-1}$, find the separation between two equipotential surfaces whose potentials differ by $125\text{ V}$. Also find the work done in moving a charge $4 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}$ along one of these surfaces.

options.A:
(i) For equal $|\Delta V|$ in uniform $E$, $d=\frac{|\Delta V|}{E}$ is constant, so equipotential surfaces are equally spaced.
(ii) $d=\frac{125}{2.5\times10^3}=5.0\times10^{-2}\,\text{m}$ and work along either surface is $0$
options.B:
(i) Equipotential surfaces are equally spaced because potential is the same everywhere.
(ii) $d=0.50\,\text{m}$ and work is $5.0\times10^{-4}\,\text{J}$
options.C:
(i) Equal potential differences require unequal spacings in uniform field.
(ii) $d=2.0\times10^{-2}\,\text{m}$ and work is $0$
options.D:
(i) Equipotential surfaces are equally spaced only for zero electric field.
(ii) $d=5.0\times10^{-2}\,\text{m}$ and work is $5.0\times10^{-4}\,\text{J}$
